guide.heading: Know Your Pour

guide.goldenRuleLine2: If a restaurant charges you $18/glass for a $45 bottle, that's 5 glasses at $9 cost each.
guide.goldenRuleLine3: If you're getting less than 5oz, you're being shorted. Period.

knowledge.heading: Wine Knowledge
knowledge.subheading: Everything you need to know to be a savvy wine drinker.
knowledge.pair1Wine: Bold reds: Cabernet Sauvignon, Malbec, Syrah. Tannins cut through fat.
knowledge.pair2Wine: Crisp whites: Sauvignon Blanc, Chablis, Muscadet. Acidity complements fish.
knowledge.pair3Wine: Italian reds: Chianti, Barbera, Sangiovese. Acidity matches tomato.
knowledge.pair4Wine: Off-dry whites: Riesling, Gewürztraminer. Sweetness tames heat.
knowledge.pair5Wine: Match intensity. Soft cheese = light wine. Aged cheese = bold wine.
knowledge.pair6Wine: Wine should be sweeter than dessert. Port, Sauternes, late harvest.
knowledge.shortPourHeading: How to Tell If Your Pour Is Short
knowledge.short1Body: Standard pour = about 2 fingers width in a standard red wine glass. Less than 1.5 fingers? You're being shorted.
knowledge.short2Body: Pick up the glass. 5oz of wine should have noticeable weight. If it feels empty, it probably is.
knowledge.short3Body: If they pour more than 5-6 glasses from a bottle, each pour is under 5oz. Watch the bottle.
knowledge.short4Body: In a proper pour, swirling should show wine reaching the widest part of the bowl. If it barely moves, it's too little.
knowledge.corkageBody: Bringing your own bottle (BYO) means paying a corkage fee, typically $25–75. It's worth it if your bottle costs significantly less than the restaurant's markup. Etiquette: Always offer the sommelier a taste. Don't bring a wine the restaurant already sells. Some restaurants waive corkage if you also buy a bottle from their list.
knowledge.term1Def: Compounds that create a drying sensation. Higher in red wines. Softens with age.
knowledge.term2Def: How heavy/full the wine feels. Light (Pinot Grigio) to full (Cabernet).
knowledge.term3Def: The environment where grapes grow: soil, climate, altitude. Makes each wine unique.
knowledge.term4Def: The year the grapes were harvested. Not all years are equal.
knowledge.term5Def: Pouring wine into a vessel to aerate it. Opens up flavors in young bold reds.
knowledge.term6Def: Droplets running down the glass after swirling. Indicates alcohol/sugar content.
knowledge.term7Def: Wine contaminated by TCA. Smells like wet cardboard. Send it back.
knowledge.term8Def: Wine made primarily from one grape variety (e.g., 100% Chardonnay).
knowledge.term9Def: Trained wine professional. Your ally in getting a proper pour.
knowledge.term10Def: The taste that lingers after swallowing. Long finish = quality wine.

about.calloutBody: If a restaurant is getting six or seven glasses out of a bottle, every customer is being shorted. That's not economy — that's theft.
